title: HaloGuard 2.0: An Open-Weights Constitutional Output Guard for Multilingual Response Safety
abstract: arXiv:2611.02134v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An input guard decides whether a request reaches the model, but never sees what the model says. Harm that emerges during generation, because a jailbreak passed the input layer or a benign request drifted into operational detail, is visible only on the output side and only as tokens arrive. We present HaloGuard 2.0, an open-weight streaming output guard that assigns a safe/unsafe probability to every response token in a single forward pass, so a deployment can stop the stream once harm is confirmed. The guard reuses the constitution of HaloGuard 1.0, our input guard, to organise a 478,532-response training corpus, and supervises each token from the point where the response becomes harmful. We find that a guard trained on conventionally shaped data learns a shortcut specific to streaming: it judges the prompt instead of the response, and handles only 13.9% of matched safe/unsafe response pairs correctly. We correct this with a second phase

translated_title: HaloGuard 2.0：面向多语言响应安全的开放权重宪法式输出守卫
translated_abstract: 输入守卫决定一个请求能否到达模型，但永远看不到模型实际说了什么。在生成过程中涌现的危害——无论是越狱攻击绕过了输入防线，还是良性请求逐渐演变为可操作的危险细节——只有在输出端、且随着token逐个到达时才能被察觉。我们提出了HaloGuard 2.0，一个开放权重的流式输出守卫，它在单次前向传播中为每个响应token分配安全/不安全概率，使部署方能够在确认危害的瞬间停止输出流。该守卫复用我们输入守卫HaloGuard 1.0的宪法（constitution）来组织包含478,532条响应的训练语料库，并从响应变为有害的那一刻起对每个token进行监督。我们发现，用传统形态数据训练的守卫会学到一种流式场景特有的捷径：它判断的是提示词而非响应本身，在匹配的安全/不安全响应对中仅能正确处理13.9%。我们通过第二阶段（训练）纠正了这一问题。
tldr: 提出开放权重的流式输出安全守卫HaloGuard 2.0，可在单次前向传播中为每个响应token实时判定安全/不安全概率，从源头拦截生成过程中才显现的危害内容，并揭示了传统数据训练会导致守卫只看提示词不看响应的流式捷径问题。
en_tdlr: HaloGuard 2.0 is an open-weights streaming output guard that assigns a safe/unsafe probability to every response token in a single forward pass, enabling real-time detection and termination of harm that emerges during generation while addressing the streaming shortcut where conventional training causes guards to judge the prompt instead of the response.
